Two of the three fixes are correct. Counting started periods with `(days_late + 29) // 30` and rounding half-up with `+ 5000` before `// 10000` both match the docstring.

The third change, swapping the minimum and the cap, is wrong. The docstring says to raise the fee to the 500-cent minimum first, then cap it at balance // 5, and that "the cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee." The new code caps first and then applies `max(fee, 500)`, so the minimum always wins, which is the opposite. The PR description says the swap "ensures the cap always wins." That's false; the code does the reverse.

The swap was made only to get `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` (`late_fee_cents(1800, 45) == 500`) to pass, and that test contradicts the docstring. Following the docstring: the fee is 54 cents, the minimum raises it to 500, and the cap brings it down to 360. The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth, so the code should keep the documented order. The conflicting test should be reported to the teammate instead of the code being changed to fit it. As written, this change also charges customers with small balances more than the documented 20% cap.

Please restore the order `max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS)` then `min(fee, balance_cents // 5)`, flag the conflicting test for the teammate, and fix the PR description.
